p: Today we’re open-sourcing PlanOpticon, our video analysis and knowledge extraction tool. It’s MIT licensed, available on PyPI, and ships with standalone binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Point PlanOpticon at any video — meeting recordings, training sessions, conference talks, screen shares — and it extracts:

list: Diagrams detected and recreated as editable Mermaid code
Action items with assignees and deadlines
A knowledge graph of entities and relationships
Reports in Markdown, HTML, and PDF

p: It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini. Set whichever API keys you have; it auto-discovers models and routes each task to the best available provider. Transcription can run locally with Whisper — no API needed.

We’ve written about this in detail over the past week (Part 1, Part 2, Part 3). The short version: recorded meetings are the largest untapped source of institutional knowledge in most organizations, and nobody has time to rewatch them.
